articleTitle: A New Robot-Based System for In-Pipe Ultrasonic Inspection of Pressure Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: As pressure pipelines are usually mounted overhead or buried underground, the in-pipe inspection equipment that can run through inside pipelines is strongly demanded. Currently, the application of robotic systems for pressure pipelines in-pipe inspection is considered as one of the most attractive solutions available. Therefore, a new robot-based system for pressure pipelines in-pipe inspection was developed. A new defect detection method for pressure pipes was presented based on ultrasonic phased array technique. The developed system mainly included three parts: a tracked mobile robot for providing the driving force of the system movement, a camera used to photograph the inner surface videos or photos inside pipelines and an ultrasonic phased array module for defects detection. The structure characteristics of water/steel interface was investigated, as well as the focusing performance of convex phased array. The detection parameters such as elements size and dynamic apertures were studied and optimized with CIVA simulations. The in-pipe inspection experiments in pressure pipelines with an outer diameter of 219 mm were also carried out. The results show that the robot-based system could successfully go through inside the pressure pipelines and the ultrasonic phased array technique could implement inner surface scanning and defect detecting, which indicates that the new defect detection method can improve the pressure pipelines inspection effect.

articleTitle: Active Thermographic Structural Feature Inspection of Wind-Turbine Rotor
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Checking wind turbines for damage is a common problem for operators of wind parks, as regular inspections are legally required in many countries and prevention is economically viable. While some of the common forms of damage are easily visible on the surface, structural problems can remain invisible for years before they eventually result in catastrophic failure of a rotor blade. Common forms of testing fibre composite parts like ultrasonic testing or X-ray tests are impractical due to the large dimensions of wind turbine components and their limited accessibility for any short-range methods. Active thermographic inspection of wind turbines is a promising approach to testing for structural flaws beneath the surface of rotor blades. As part of an ongoing research project, a setup for testing the general viability of this method was built and used to compare different thermographic cameras. A sample cut from a discarded rotor blade was modified to emulate structural damage. The results are promising for the development of a cost effective on-site testing system.

articleTitle: Abnormal Target Detection of High-Speed Train's Roof
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Safety inspections are an eternal theme for high-speed trains. Routine detection methods by inspectors have many disadvantages, and so a method based on digital image processing to detect abnormal targets is introduced in this paper. Considering the length of the train, an image acquisition and stitching method are presented. Since the image we obtain is not aligned to the standard one owing to different speeds, an improved template matching algorithm is proposed to align the two images roughly, and an enhanced correlation coefficient algorithm (ECC) is adopted for precise alignment. Last, an image comparing algorithm based on structural similarity (SSIM) is proposed to detect abnormal targets.

articleTitle: Wheel Tread Defects Inspection Based on SVM
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The wheel, rolling part of the train, is closely related to the safety operation. When the wheel tread is flawed, strong impact vibration will be produced. That not only can cause serious damage of the wheel-rail system, but also reduce passenger comfort. In this paper, a system of collecting wheel tread defect image was designed, that be used in the online running train. The system can identify and locate the wheel tread defects accurately such as wheel tread flat, wheel tread spalling and other defects.

articleTitle: The Pre-Processing of Ultrasonic Array Data for Time-Reversal-Based Imaging Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultrasonic time-reversal-based imaging algorithm is a typical super resolution imaging method for detecting and imaging point-like defects embedded in a homogeneous medium in the field of Nondestructive evaluation (NDE). In this paper, a pre-processing method for extracting the valid scattered signals, reflected by the defects in the test structure, from pulse-echo time traces under the noisy case is proposed. A sub-area containing the defects is approximately assessed firstly via the conventional beamforming imaging algorithm, and then the gating point of window function is calculated, which can be applied to extract the valid scattered signals even when they are totally covered by the background noise. This proposed method is tested with experimental ultrasonic array data collected using the full matrix capture process. The experimental result implemented on a block of copper with two side-drilled holes (SDHs) shows that the proposed pre-processing method can extract the scattered signals from the pulse-echo time traces. Then multi-frequency time-reversal with multiple signal classification (MF-TR-MUSIC) over a given frequency range is applied to obtain the ultrasonic image of copper sample. According to the imaging result, the two SDHs can be located successfully.

articleTitle: Existing Weld Seam Recognition Based on Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, the image processing method is adopted to recognize the weld seam. A set of weld seam recognition system is built. The software part of the system is introduced as steps of image preprocessing, edge detection and image post-processing. The anisotropic filtering is used to remove the image noise, at the same time, it maintains the edge of the image as much as possible. Then the Canny operator is applied to obtain the edge of the weld seam. Finally the morphology operation is performed to extract the weld seam field. The experiment part compares the weld seam recognition accuracy and the average running time in four cases.

articleTitle: Reseach on Application of Air Coupled Ultrasonic Surface Wave Detection
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In the nondestructive testing of in-service gas pipeline, it is not applicable to use common coupling method. However, air coupled ultrasonic testing is an effective coupling method. This work presents an application of air coupled ultrasonic detection. Firstly, the basic principle and theory of air coupled ultrasonic testing technology are introduced, and the attenuation law of ultrasonic wave in air is analyzed, then the air coupled ultrasonic surface wave detection system is set up. Experiment is carried out on a testing block with a number of cracks, the result verifies the feasibility of detection system.

articleTitle: Characterisation of Steel Corrosion Using High Frequency RFID
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The progression characterisation of exposed atmospheric corrosion on metal substrates is a major problem in the field of corrosion science and Non-destructive Evaluation (NDE). High frequency radio frequency identification (HF RFID) sensors are attractive in diverse applications where sensor performance is needed at a low cost and dimension restriction. An approach adapting commercial passive 13.56MHz RFID tags for sensing corrosion stage has been developed. The investigation includes balance of sensing and positioning of RFID sensors for corrosion detection by analysing real part and imaginary part of the complex impedance. With passive RFID sensors, real part and imaginary part of complex impedance are extracted from the reader coil with Vector network analyser (VNA) and delivering a unique capability for corrosion sensing with different atmospheric exposure time steel samples (1 month, 6 months, 10 months and 12 months). The relationship between these features and corrosion exposed time has been derived which is useful for corrosion progression measurement, early stage corrosion monitoring and prediction in industrial fields such as the marine industry.

articleTitle: Bilateral Laser Vision Tracking Synchronous Inspection Robotic System
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: For inspecting welding seams of large-scale equipment such as storage tanks and spherical tanks, it usually cost much manpower and material, while automated testing robot can achieve fast and accurate detection. Because X-ray Flat Panel Detector is dependent on specialized automated equipment, it can greatly enhance X-ray inspection technology in large storage tanks that applying the Mecanum Omnidirectional Mobile Robot into automated weld detection. In this paper, an X-ray Flat Panel Detector based wall-climbing robotic system is developed for intelligent detecting of welding seams. The robot system consists of two Mecanum vehicles equipped with either a Flat Panel Detector or an X -ray generator and climbing on both side of the tank wall. Inspection robot can carry detector stably with reliable suction force and adapt to different surfaces. To let the X-ray Flat Panel Detector work properly, laser vision tracking system is used to ensure synchronous operation of the two robots. Some experiment was conducted and reported.

articleTitle: Design of Eddy Current Probe with TMR Components for Detection of Inner Defects in Thin Metallic Structure
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Non Destructive testing (NDT) methods have a wide field of application in manufacturing and maintenance industries. Inner defect detection in conductive plates represents an important issue in NDT. Base on theoretical analysis of eddy current technique, Probe with TMR (Tunneling Magneto Resistance), components is designed to detect this kind of inner defect. By selecting the position of maximum variation where TMR is fixed, the inner defects 2mm beneath metal surface can be detected. The simulation results indicated the design of No-differential where TMR is fixed on the top to excitation winding is the optimum design in term of the variation of amplitude magnetic field. The work is significant, which could provide theoretic guidance in manufacturing probe and experiment.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic TOFD Imaging of Weld Flaws Using Wavelet Transforms and Image Registration
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Ultrasonic TOFD is an effective weld crack inspection technique. The signal-to-ratio(SNR) of TOFD image is low due to the intensity of diffraction wave is rather weak compared with the lateral wave and the bottom echo wave. A method is comprised of two steps that contains wavelet shrinkage and image registration is investigated to reduce the noise and improve the resolution of TOFD images. Using wavelet multi-resolution analysis to split the data into the components with different frequency resolution, and a modified threshold function is established to adjust the wavelet coefficients. To eliminate the error in TOFD images generated by randomly setting of the probe initial positions, image registration based on maximum correlation is adopted in the processing of each TOFD image, then the processed images are added together to form a new TOFD image with high definition and SNR. In order to evaluate the reliability of proposed method, we have established the experiment system, and sampled a number of TOFD data with randomly distributed noise. We adopted one-dimension wavelet transform and two-dimension wavelet transform in the very beginning of the first step of the proposed algorithm respectively. The SNR of the result obtained in this step is improved significantly compared with the classic algorithms. After the registered, images have been added to form a new one, it comes to the final result that shows not only the SNR but also the definition of the image is enhanced effectively. The defect characteristics are much easier to be identified.

articleTitle: The Use of Multi-Mode TFM to Measure the Depth of Small Surface-Break Cracks in Welds
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, small crack (depth = 1 mm) initiated from top surface of welds are imaged and characterized using ultrasonic array. The conventional Total Focusing Method (TFM), which allows the array to be focused at every point in the target region in both transmission and reception, is a post-processing imaging algorithm of ultrasonic array data. The TFM can be also implemented combining a variety of propagation modes and several types of waves, involving longitudinal waves and shear waves. Due to the small cracks near the top surface where the array located, no reflection from crack faces or root and tip indications are observed in the image formed using conventional TFM imaging algorithm, which includes only direct ray paths between the array and image points. For this case, it is challenge to size the small cracks initiated from top surface. This paper presents three modes of wave propagation for the TFM imaging to inspect and measure the depth of the small cracks with greater reliability than conventional TFM imaging.

articleTitle: Hybrid RFEC and Transmission NDT for Detection of Lead-Steel Multilayers
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Lead-steel multilayered material has high thickness and is bonded of layers of ferromagnetic metal and non-ferromagnetic metal. Hence, it is challenging to inspect inner defects in steel layers. To achieve simultaneous inspection, a hybrid remote-field eddy current testing (RFECT) and transmitting-receiving (TR) testing method has been proposed and validated through numerical simulations. This testing system contains both UTC-based RFEC and transmission probes. To get satisfactory sensibilities of defects of different sizes at different depths, parameters of the probes are optimized through simulations. The mean sensibilities of 4 given crack positions of the optimized model have increased 1.84,1.91,3.926 and 0.714%. In addition, the simulation result can be used to supervise experiment investigation.

articleTitle: Current Trends in Digital Industrial Radiography - from Nano to Macro Scale -
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Industrial digital radiography (DIR) substitutes the classical film radiography. Film is substituted by imaging plates and digital detector arrays (DDA). New parameters as SNR and CNR and basic spatial resolution (SR<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>) need to be considered and understood. This is the precondition for extended and automated application as dimensional measurement and automated defect recognition (ADR). Modern fast Computed Tomography (CT) units are implemented in the quality assurance process for at-line and in-line inspection in industry. The scope of typical CT applications is extended from flaw detection to dimensional measurement in industry substituting coordinate measurement machines. Mobile computed tomography is applied for in-service radiographic crack detection and sizing of welded pipes in nuclear power plants and for NDT of large CFRP structures of airplanes. Small structures of integrated electronic circuits and compact electronic packages are visualized and measured with μ-CT or lens based nano CT systems. Phase contrast imaging provides enhanced structure contrast in micro radiography and micro CT.

articleTitle: NDT for Characterizing Ageing and Degradation of Nuclear Power Plant Materials - Fatigue and Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Following the design rules and considering the safety factors, the lifetime of nuclear power plants (NPP), worldwide is expected to be in the range of 40 years. Obviously, within such a lifespan the components and systems under heavy mechanical (static and dynamic pressure, vibration), thermic and irradiation loads, suffer ageing phenomena which are Thermal Ageing, Corrosion, Low Cycle Fatigue (LCF), High Cycle Fatigue(HCF), Very high Cycle Fatigue (VHCF) and Irradiation Damage due to neutrons - and the possible synergy of the phenomena together. However, the electrical power producing utilities as operators of the NPP, perform a `predictive maintenance', also called `retrofitting', by timely performing the replacement of especially stressed components. Examples for these replacement procedures are the change of heat-exchangers and parts of the main cooling pipes, like hot knees near heat-exchangers or components of the surge-line in pressurized-water NPP. As the components, which are replaced, always are manufactured according the newest technical state of the art, the retrofitting enhances inherently also the safety standard. In Germany, where due to the Atomic Law, the safety of the plants is asked for, this law - beside economic reasons of a higher technical availability - is the driver for replacement. The IAAEA has introduced safety standards for Ageing Management and according these documents, worldwide most of the atomic energy producing countries have adopted their national guidelines, newly introducing mainly fatigue condition monitoring. The proposed paper discusses, on one hand, the application of the 3MA-strategy (Micromagnetic, Multiparameter, Microstructure and Stress Analysis) on ferromagnetic components and Eddy-Current-based and Ultrasonic techniques on austenitic materials for early-characterizing fatigued microstructures - before cracking and, on the other hand, characterization of irradiation damage in pressure-vessel steels.

articleTitle: Weld Defect Detection Using High Frequency SH Guided Wave Transducers Based on Magnetostrictive Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In view of the low sensitivity to defects of low-frequency shear horizontal (SH) guided wave transducers, a high frequency SH-guided-wave transducer is designed. The guided wave modes that could be excited in high frequency are analyzed based on frequency bandwidth and spatial period. Based on the pitch-catch transducers, an experiment platform is set up and weld defects are detected. The waveforms in time domain are analyzed according to the velocity of each guided wave mode and the relative position between transducers and the weld. Finally, the weld is scanned using the designed SH-guided-wave transducers, and the image of the weld is obtained. The result shows that the transducers can effectively detect the actual defects in weld.

articleTitle: On the Possibility of Use of Fractional Order Derivatives to Eddy Current Non-Destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The paper presents the possibility of using the fractional derivetives in non-destructive testing when eddy currents method is applied.

articleTitle: Recent Developments of Photon Counting and Energy Discriminating Detectors for Radiographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The direct detection of X-ray photons into electrical signals is enabled by usage of highly absorbing photo conducting materials (e.g. CdTe) as detection layer of an underlying CMOS semiconductor X-ray image detector. If the read-out speed is high enough (ca. 50 - 100 ns dead time) single X-ray photons can be counted and their energy measured. Read-out noise and dark image correction can be diminished. By setting energy thresholds, selected energy ranges of the X-ray spectrum can be detected or suppressed. This allows material discrimination or reduction of scattered radiation, which results in an enhanced contrast sensitivity.

articleTitle: Research on the Detection Mechanism of Crack with Corrosion Using Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In the running process of locomotive, many tiny cracks emerge on the wheel tread due to the rolling contact between wheel and rail. On account of being exposed to complex environment, the crack flank will be corroded and filled with a third medium such as corrosion, then contact with each other under cyclic tensile or compressive stress, leading to local closure of the crack region, which affects the physical properties of the crack, showing low electrical conductivity for example. This is a new phenomenon that conventional electromagnetic detection method might not be capable of detecting such defects effectively. This paper aims to detect crack with corrosion on the basis of eddy current pulsed thermography (ECPT), establish a composite crack model to explore the performance of ECPT over low conductivity crack, and the influence of varying electromagnetic properties to ECPT will be studied as well. Crack detection principle was introduced first, and numerical simulations were conducted to detect crack with corrosion, transient and spatial temperature distribution characteristics were extracted during heating and cooling stage, experiments were designed and conducted to verify the accuracy and consistency.

articleTitle: Robotic NDT for Turbine Blades Based on the Transverse Waves
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The defects located on the curved surface are difficult to be distinguished by the traditional reflected echo waves, in this paper, the transverse wave is applied to test those micro-cracks, which near to the test surface. A high recurrence positional accurate robotic manipulator is used for manipulating the test object so that the positional accuracy of robotic scanning trajectory can be guaranteed, as well as the incident angle and ultrasonic propagation length. Signal to noise ratio of ultrasonic A-scan waves is improved when the constraint parameters are correct, moreover, ultrasonic C-scan image is offered to the inspector to gain the nondestructive evaluation conclusion. Experimental results indicate the crack with minimize width of 0.15 mm that can be identified by the proposed robotic NDT system, when the oblique incident test method is used, the transverse waves can be excited so that the characteristic of defects can be displayed in the C-scan image.

articleTitle: Welding Defects Detection and Classification by Using Eddy Current Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In welding process, many factors will lead to welding defects which could be lack of penetration, lack of fusion, slag, gas pole and crack. In this paper, eddy current thermography has been employed to inspect welding defects in metal parts. Several parts which were prepared have different type of welding defect in each. The experiment system was introduced following the introduction of specimens. The Infra images captured with Infra camera during the test process were analyzed using MATLAB to discover the temperature characteristics of welding defects. Graphics of the temperature distribution of defects were presented. According to the temperature features of defects, the welding defects in metal parts were classified. The results show that eddy current thermography is effective to detect three types of defects in the specimens, of which two types can be identified.

articleTitle: Application of FTP in Rail Profile and Surface Flaw Detection Based on Orthogonal Two-Frequency Composite Grating
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to reconstruct the rail profile and flaws on the rail surface, we aim to use the improved Fourier Transform Profilometry (FTP) based on the orthogonal two-frequency composite grating. The different modulation information caused by the rail profile and surface flaws can be obtained by the same frame of deformed fringe pattern of composite grating. After a basic process of FTP, the rail profile and flaws on the surface can be respectively reconstructed from the wrapping phase of the low frequency and high frequency. It is easier to perform the phase unwrapping from the spectrum with a lower frequency and longer equivalent wavelength, but the accuracy of measurement is inversely proportional to the equivalent wavelength. Accordingly, the accuracy of the image recovered with high frequency is higher than that recovered with the low one. So the rail shape is reconstructed from the low frequency part of the composite grating and the surface flaws are reconstructed from the high part, both with high accuracy. Simulations, error analysis and experiments were made. Results show that FTP based on the orthogonal two-frequency composite grating can meet the need of the actual measurement in the detection of the rail profile and surface flaws.

articleTitle: Multi-Channel Wideband Torsional Mode MPT Based on Phased Array Technology for SHM of Pipes
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Recently, the application of magnetostrictive patch transducers (MPTs) has gradually extended to structural health monitoring of pipeline (SHM). However, it is limited in this field due to demagnetization and fixed working frequency of traditional transducers. To solve these problems, a novel torsional mode MPT using permanent magnet array and four solenoid coils is proposed for structural health monitoring of pipe. In the suggested configuration, each solenoid coil can generate and receive torsional guided wave of any frequency because its width is far less than wavelength. And the phased array method is adopted to control the propagation direction of guided wave. Furthermore, it is experimentally verified that the 4-channel wideband MPT can inspect a 3% circumferential defect of pipe using torsional guided waves with different frequencies from 30 kHz to 200 kHz.

articleTitle: Research on Ultrasonic Imaging of Oblique Cracks with Angle Probe
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Oblique crack is one of the common defects in industrial ultrasonic testing. The angle probe can detect oblique defects more efficiently. The path of the ultrasonic wave in the multi-layer medium can be calculated by the ray tracing technique. Then it can be used in synthetic aperture imaging algorithm for improving ultrasonic imaging resolution. In this paper, the new forward interpretation algorithm is used to image the internal oblique crack. The better result is shown in comparing with the traditional SAFT algorithm for straight probe.

articleTitle: Development of Electromagnetic Nondestructive Testing for Inspecting Mechanical Lap Joint of High-Temperature Superconducting Tapes
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: To facilitate construction and maintenance of nuclear fusion reactors, a remountable (demountable) high-temperature superconducting magnet was proposed. The magnet is assembled from several segments with mechanical joints. The electrical resistance of joint (joint resistance) at cryogenic temperature has great influence on the performance of the magnet, a nondestructive testing technique at room temperature is highly demanded to predict joint resistance. In this study, the electrical characteristics of the joint were focused on to develop an electromagnetic NDT technique for inspecting the joint. To identify the factors relating to the joint resistance and the correlation between the electrical characteristics, the cross sections of the joint were observed and the electrical resistance and impedance of the joint were measured. The result indicated a small air gap existing in the joint that could possibly be the cause for increment in joint resistance, though the degree of influence of such gap could not be evaluated over measured electrical resistance and impedance result. Causal analyses were conducted by numerical models, which indicated arranging the current perpendicular to the joint surface is effective for inspecting the joint. Then additional numerical analyses were conducted to evaluate the feasibility of applying the direct measurement and eddy current testing for inspection. The result showed the possibility of detecting particular air gap, optimization of the measurement condition is required.

articleTitle: Wireless Vibration Monitoring System for Rail Base Defect of Switch Turnout
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Due to asymmetrical structure and motion working state of rail turnout, it is difficult to monitor turnout defect by conventional techniques. In this paper, a wireless vibration monitoring system was proposed for monitoring rail base defect, which could realize two kinds of active and passive working patterns. Multi-energy of solar and vibration could achieve charging for sensor node. Energy management technology was applied for energy conservation. The experimental results showed the proposed wireless Structure Health Monitoring(SHM) system can detect existence of defect and longer defect has larger amplitude.

articleTitle: Recognition of Key Targets of Locomotive Bottom Based on 3D Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a new method is designed to recognize the key targets of the locomotive bottom based on the 3D point cloud data. In this method, the key points were selected on the basis of ISS (Intrinsic Shape Signatures) algorithm, the feature descriptors were constructed using FPFH (Fast Point Feature Histograms) algorithm, and the recognition and localization of the targets were conducted by the combination of template matching and cluster analysis. The experiment was carried out on bolts for validation. Experimental results verified the effectiveness of the proposed method and proved the feasibility of recognition and localization of key targets of the locomotive bottom based on 3D point cloud data.

articleTitle: Influence of Focal Length on Focusing Performance of EMAT Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) phased arrays consist of multiple independent elements. The steering and focusing of the beam can be achieved by individually controlling the time delay of each element. The diameter of focal spot and the pressure distribution of the steering direction play an important role in determining the performance of the beam focusing. The pressure distribution of focusing beam would change into that of steering beam when the distance of focal length is large enough. By comparing the radiation patterns of the various focal lengths in the near field, it is learned that a short focal length is beneficial to the energy concentration and is helpful to improve the resolution of the system. The validity of the simulation model is verified by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Ensemble Bayesian Tensor Factorization for Debond Thermal NDT
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: One of the common types of defects in the carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) is debond. The different feature extraction algorithms of optical stimulated infrared thermography are used to obtained the debond detection. However, the low detection accuracy as well as remain as challenges. In this paper, the ensemble variational Bayes tensor factorization (EVBTF) has been proposed to overcome the problems. The framework of the proposed algorithm is based on the Bayesian learning theory. It constructs spatial-transient multi-layer mining structure. Experimental tests have been proved that it can effectively improve the contrast ratio between the defective areas and the sound areas.

articleTitle: 3-D Simulation for the Acoustic Field Directivity of SH-Wave EMATs
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The advantages of SH guided waves are that their dispersion characteristics are simple, and the distortion is low when they pass through austenitic welds, thus their application prospect in the non -destructive testing is great. The acoustic field directivity of SH-wave electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) affects the detection performance. However, the acoustic field distribution of SH-wave EMATs cannot be obtained by a 2-D simulation model. 3-D finite element models of SH guided waves generated by periodic permanent magnet (PPM) EMATs are presented based on COMSOL. The simulation results show that the acoustic field direction angle of SH guided waves is 16.7°. The accuracy of the simulation model is verified by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Shear Wave Purity in Spiral Coil EMATs for Defects Testing in Non-Ferromagnetic Metal Material
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In some mainly shear wave electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) such as spiral coil EMATs, an existing longitudinal wave distorts the shear wave response and complicates the echo pattern. In order to enhance the shear wave purity, a finite element model has been developed for predicting the eddy current, the static and dynamic magnetic fields in an aluminum specimen. And a method of predicting the shear wave purity is introduced based on the predicted fields. The effects of an impedance matching network and a band-pass filter on the bulk wave amplitudes in the ultrasonic receiving system were investigated by experiments. Subsequently, the influences of magnet dimensions and the thickness of Si -steel backplate on shear wave purity were also studied. Results indicate that a band-pass filter and an impedance matching network designed at a center frequency that is the same as the excitation current, a larger diameter and smaller thickness magnet, and a thicker Si-steel back-plate can help to improve the shear wave purity, but it is at some sacrifice of the shear wave sensitivity.

articleTitle: An Experimental Platform for Electromagnetic Ultrasonic Guided Wave Tomography Technique
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Electromagnetic ultrasonic guided wave tomography technique combines electromagnetic ultrasonic nondestructive testing with guided wave tomography technology, which can gain lots of visual information of defects in plates and improve the accuracy of testing. This paper presents an experimental platform which utilizes electromagnetic acoustic transducers to generate and receive Lamb wave and reconstructs the profile of defects of plate. This platform is significant for evaluating the design of electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) and various tomography algorithms. This experimental platform consists of transmitting and receiving circuits generating and receiving ultrasonic guided waves, data acquisition circuit collecting ultrasonic signal, FPGA circuits controlling the operation of the platform, a mechanical structure supporting test pieces, a motion module and positioning modules precisely detecting the positions of EMATs at different spatial sampling points. The working parameters of the platform are controlled by a laptop, and the received signals are displayed on the laptop as well. The software for the platform is developed based on LabWindows/CVI. A 2 mm thick aluminum plate with a blind hole with a diameter of 26 mm and a depth of 1 mm is scanned by the platform. The blind hole is reconstructed using tomography technique, which validates the effectiveness of the platform.

articleTitle: Hybrid of TSR and Seeded Region Growing for Debonding Detection Using Optical Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) are commonly used in the field of aerospace. Under manufacturing or in service procedure, there exists internal defects such as delamination and debonding due to the factors of improper production and environment. In order to guarantee CFRP internal quality and safety, the optical pulsed thermography (OPT) nondestructive testing has been used to detect the internal defects. However, the current OPT related methods has problems of uneven illumination and low resolution of defects detection. In this paper, the hybrid of thermographic signal reconstruction (TSR) and seeded region growing (SRG) algorithm was proposed to deal with the infrared thermal image sequences of the CFRP specimen, which can significantly enhance the detection rate. Finally, the event based F-score is computed to measure the detection results and comparison studies show that the proposed method can improve the performance of the detection.

articleTitle: Circumferential Current Field Testing Method for Innerwall Cracks Detection in Aluminum Tube
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel circumferential current field testing method for the detection of innerwall cracks in aluminum tube. The finite element method (FEM) model of the circumferential current field testing method is proposed to analyze the electromagnetic field around the crack. The circumferential current field testing probe with tunnel magneto resistance (TMR) sensor array and testing system are developed. The inner-wall crack detection experiments are carried out. The results show that the inner-wall cracks in aluminum tube can be detected, positioned and evaluated by the circumferential current field testing method.

articleTitle: Spatial-Time-Step Features Fusion Algorithm in Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Eddy Current Pulsed Thermograph (ECPT) has received extensive attention due to high sensitivity detection with surface and subsurface cracks. However, it has unsolved detection problem of blind defect location without any prior knowledge. This paper presents a spatial-time-step features fusion algorithm to obtain defects reconstruction of whole specimen by blind scanning. The proposed method is intended to use features extraction by independent component analysis (ICA) and features selection by skewness. Finally, the optimal feature of each step is fused to obtain defects reconstruction image by using common orthogonal basis extraction (COBE). Experiments have been conducted to validate this study and it shows that this algorithm has a great effect on feature selection.

articleTitle: Scatter Imaging - Simulation of Aperture Focusing by Deconvolution
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: X-ray scatter imaging is a well-established NDT technique to inspect complex objects using only a single-sided access. We present a specially designed multi-slit scatter camera consisting of several twisted slits which are parallelly arranged in a metal block. The camera projects one image per slit to the digital detector array, where the images are overlaying each other. The aperture is corrected based on a deconvolution algorithm to focus the overlaying projections into a single representation of the object. To achieve high scatter intensities from an object, it is necessary to optimize the parameters of the scatter system by simulation.

articleTitle: Simulation of High Frequency Ultrasonic Field in Multilayer Medium
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: To analyze the ultrasonic field characteristics of high frequency focused transducer in medium, the Gaussian Beam Equivalent Point Source of acoustic field is established by utilizing the advantages of Point Source Superposition Model and Multi-Gaussian Model, and the acoustic field simulation of high frequency focused transducer is conducted. The acoustic field distributions of high frequency focused beam in liquid-solid medium and multilayer medium are studied with this model and calculation and simulation are conducted. Thus, the theoretical basis is provided for the propagation of high frequency ultrasound in medium.

articleTitle: EMD of EMAT NDT in X70 Pipeline Weld Defects
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) is an emerging non-destructive testing technique which has been applied to the pipelines inspection. EMAT has advantages of Non coupling agent and can be used with high temperature environment. Due to the roughness remaining in surface of the pipeline, the quantitative analysis of defect location are challenges by using EMAT NDT. This paper introduces a new detection method of EMAT by hybriding Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) with IMFs reconstruction to quantitative detect weld defects. The new method has been validated to detect the defects of weld for the X70 pipeline by using Bulk-wave. Experiments have been proved that it improves the accuracy of the measurement, and achieve the recognition of millimeter-level defects.

articleTitle: Research on Railway Wheel Roundness On-Board Monitoring Techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: With the increase of railway speed, the impact of wheel roundness on running safety and riding comfort becomes greater. When in high speed, high-order wheel roundness dramatically decreases the service life of vehicle components and track system. An on-board wheel roundness monitoring technique is proposed in this paper. The vibration signals are obtained by the acceleration transducers installed on the axle boxes then processed to get wheel roundness order. The method is proved to be valid by theoretical analysis and on-board experiments. At last, the relationship between train speed and vibration strength at different roundness level is also discussed.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Imaging of TGO in Thermal Barrier Coatings by Nano-CT
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Air plasma sprayed thermal barrier coatings(TBCs) with double-layer structure was investigated, and the experiment of constant temperature oxidization was performed at 1050°C The microstructure and high temperature oxidation behaviors of thermal barrier coatings were investigated with scanning electron micro-scope(SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy(EDS) and high resolution nano-CT. The results show that the bond coat is oxidized when the air plasma sprayed thermal barrier coatings after 12 hours of high temperature oxidation, and a layer of uneven thickness of thermally grown oxide(TGO) has grown between ceramic topcoat and bond coat, and the average thickness of TGO is 1.979μm by SEM. The three-dimensional structure images of the coatings are obtained by nano-CT, the internal microstructure and morphology of TGO are displayed, and the measured average thickness of TGO is 1.991μm. The results of nano-CT analysis are consistent with the results of scanning electron microscopy(SEM).

articleTitle: Nondestructive Inpsection of Carbon Fibre Reinforced Polymer Laminates Using Guided Waves
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The ultrasonic guided wave technique for carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates has received a lot of interests in recent years due to its high efficiency. In this paper, the propagation of guided waves in a 10-layer CFRP laminate is investigated. Furthermore, the interaction between guided waves and different defects in the laminate are simulated by the finite element method (FEM). Simulation shows that the first order guided wave is sensitive to the crack and interfacial debonding.

articleTitle: Research on Ultrasonic Testing and Image Preprocessing Method of Remanufactured Oil Pipe Inner Wall
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Discarded steel oil pipes can be remanufactured by Centrifugal Self-propagating High temperature Synthesis (SHS) method. A ceramic layer can be attached onto the inner wall of the steel pipe. The ceramic-lined steel composite pipes possess better wear and corrosion resisting properties as well as longer life-span, which creates huge economic benefits. However, due to electric insulation, nonferromagnetism, anisotropy, high noise and acoustic attenuation, it is difficult to detect long and narrow ceramic inner wall, which can damage service security. In this work, ultrasonic A- and C-scan was implemented on a ceramic-lined steel composite pipe. The C-scan RGB image of a test block with precast flat bottom holes was transformed into a grey-scale map. Then a contour plot was drawn for flaw edge detection. Finally, visualized images of defect locations on the test block were captured. The experiment results indicate that ultrasonic technology is adaptive for detecting ceramic-lined steel composite material from outside the pipe. The results of A-scan reflect the bonding state of ceramic and metal layers. Grey-scale map method can do effective preprocessing on C-scan images so that defects can be visualized.

articleTitle: Analysis of the High Frequency Transducer Acoustic Field Based on Gaussian Beam Equivalent Point Source
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: To study the acoustic field distribution features of high frequency focused transducer in medium, the Gaussian beam equivalent point source of acoustic field is established based on the advantages of acoustic field point source overlapping model and multi-Gaussian model, and then simulation is made to the acoustic field of high frequency focused transducer. The comparison of the simulation results of three acoustic fields of 20MHz and 50MHz high frequency focused transducers show that, the Gaussian beam equivalent point source can make rapid and effective simulation to the acoustic field of high frequency focused transducer. At last, the real acoustic field measurement is conducted to the 20MHz high frequency focused transducer. The experiment results are consistent with the simulation results of Gaussian beam equivalent point source, so that the correctness of Gaussian beam equivalent point source is verified.

articleTitle: Mobile Tomographic X-Ray Inspection
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: A special 3D tomographic algorithm was developed for mobile inspection of large objects. The method is based on a coplanar movement of an X-ray tube parallel to the surface of a digital detector array (DDA). Two different designs were developed and applied for 3D testing of welded pipes in nuclear power plants and large aircraft components made from carbon fiber reinforced polymers (CFRP). The reconstructed tomographic images permit the detection, characterization and measurement of the dimensions of flaws with enhanced sensitivity compared to conventional radiography and UT.

articleTitle: Application of Compressed Sensing on Eletromagetic Transducer Testing
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, an innovative Compressed Sensing (CS) framework has been proposed with the purpose of providing a sub-Nyquist sampling mechanism to Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducer (EMAT) testing. Particularly, a novel sparse representation method based on dictionary learning was introduced into the CS framework aimed at a more efficient signal sparse representation and more accurate signal reconstruction. The proposed CS framework was examined through a process of thickness measurement of an 813-X70 pipeline. Experimental results indicated that the thickness feature of the specimen could be precisely extracted from the recovered data with 20% of compression ratio compared with conventional sampling method. It demonstrates that the CS theorem can significantly reduce the required sampling rate of EMAT testing system without loss of signal resolution, thus improves the overall testing efficiency.

articleTitle: Power Efficient Ultrasound Imaging Diagnosis System Using Adaptive Data Prediction Scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: An adaptive-data-prediction-based (ADPB) ultrasound receiver is developed to achieve a wide dynamic range (DR) and high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) ultrasound imaging with no extra power penalty. To guarantee both high resolution and power efficiency, a digital linear predictor is introduced, which significantly enhances the resolution and eliminates the power hungry circuits in traditional receivers. With digital assisted signal processing, performance stress on analog modules including ADCs is relaxed, resulting in further reduced power consumption. To enable real-time digital signal processing, least-mean-square (LMS) algorithm is introduced. The proposed system was implemented on a FPGA-based hardware platform. The measurement results show that with a simple 10-bit ADC, it achieves 80-dB SNR, which can be usually accomplished by a state-of-art 16-bits ADC. More importantly, the elimination of TGC and the employment of low resolution ADC reduce the total power by 2-3 orders.

articleTitle: The FEM Analysis of PZT5H Piezoelectric Square Sheet Thickness Mode Vibration
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Based on the FEM (Finite Element Method) application software ANSYS 15.0, the analysis of PZT-5H piezoelectric square sheet with specific dimensions was performed. Using multi-physics fields coupling, the geometric entity was modeled and the solid 226 coupling field element was selected for meshing to get the FEM model. The modal analysis was carried out to get the simulation results, including the modal frequencies and the first ten vibration modes, and harmonic analysis was also performed to simulate the electric impedance and resonance properties. The analysis results would be valuable for high frequency piezoelectric ultrasound transducer design and fabrication.

articleTitle: Detection and Regulation Technology of Residual Stress on the Train Wheel Tread Surface
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The railway transportation plays an important role in the national economic development, as the speed of trains become faster and faster, the load capacity of trains become heavier and heavier, people pay more attention to the safety of railway transportation. The train wheel is the important part of carrying the train, it is easy to result in the mechanical damage on the wheel such as wear, crack and peel in the process of running, and these will seriously affect the safe operation of trains. This article mainly introduces a technology about detection and regulation of residual stress on the train wheel surface. By completing the relevant tensile experiment, testing experiments and controlling experiments, analyzing the results and the function of regulation. Eventually we find an effective way to detect and reduce the residual stress on the train wheel surface.

articleTitle: Probability of Detection for Fatigue Crack in Pulsed Eddy Current Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In pulsed eddy current thermography (PECT), probability of detection (POD) is one of the most important indexes to evaluate the reliability of detection. Generally, POD is defined as the probability that a crack with particular length is detected under special test condition. In this paper, a series of metal plates with different lengths of fatigue cracks were introduced to obtain the thermal response through the orthogonal experiment. A linear regression model was established to describe the relationship between thermal responses and crack lengths, and the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method was employed to achieve the specific parameters of POD model. Then, the resulting confidence interval of POD was presented based on Wald method. The research aims to provide a quantitative evaluation method for detection reliability in PECT.

articleTitle: Application of Magnetic Flux Leakage in Oil Tank Bottom
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Tank floor corrosion has been a significant risk of petroleum and petrochemical industry. For tank floor inspection, acoustic emission qualitative methods is generally in the industry, which have some problems such as lack of accuracy. In this paper, the principle of magnetic flux leakage detection was studied, and the 25 mm thickness of magnetic flux leakage detect was developed. The equipment has been well used in the enterprise, to solve the problem of storage tank floor corrosion and provide support for the enterprise.

articleTitle: A Generalized Time-Reversal-Based Imaging for Ultrasonic Nondestructive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In this paper, a generalized time-reversal-based imaging algorithm is presented and introduced into the area of ultrasonic Nondestructive evaluation (NDE) for imaging defect in solids. It can be expressed in different forms, including central frequency time-reversal with multiple signal classification (CF-TR-MUSIC), as well as its multi-frequency forms over a given frequency bandwidth, namely multi-frequency TR-MUSIC (MF-TR-MUSIC) and a related phase-coherent form (PC-MUSIC). These imaging algorithms are tested with experimental ultrasonic array data, and their performance is evaluated in terms of lateral resolution and sensitive to noise, two particularly important indicators for industrial NDE. It is shown that all three methods are capable of resolving lateral targets spaced closer than the Rayleigh limit, achieving super-resolution imaging. Both CF-TR-MUSIC and MF-TR-MUSIC can locate the positions of targets correctly, whereas the results from PC-MUSIC are less clear because of the presence of multiple peaks in the vicinity of target. However, an advantage of PC-MUSIC is that it can overcome the elongated point spread function that appears in TR-MUSIC images, and hence provide enhanced axial resolution. For high noise levels, MF-TR-MUSIC and PC-MUSIC are shown to provide stable image and suppress the presence of artifacts seen in the CF-TR-MUSIC image.

articleTitle: Effects of Interlamianr Electrical Behavior on Eddy Currents in Carbon Fiber Composite Materials
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to thoroughly investigate interlaminar contact resistivity and its influence on eddy current (EC) in carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. Contact resistivity between adjacent laminae, together with the anisotropic bulk conductivity of a single-layer lamina, were measured. The measured values were then utilized in finite element (FE) models to study the effect of interlaminar electrical behavior on eddy currents in CFRPs. The numerically simulation results showed that eddy currents are highly concentrated around the interface between angled laminae when contact resistivity is taken into account, while a significant attenuation of the currents occurs in a noncontact model. The numerical results were verified by comparing the calculated voltages with the experimentally measured ones. It was found that the FE results considering contact resistivity are in accordance with experimental ones and will allow a better interfacial modeling of CFRPs.

articleTitle: Statistical Properties of Barkhausen Noise with 180° Domain Wall for Stress Characterization
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This paper develops an intergrate system of Magnetic optical imaging with Magnetic Barkhausen noise (MBN) measurement system to synchronize the in-situ view of both micro and macro magnetic properties in grain oriented electrical steel. Statistical properties of Magnetic Barkhausen Noise (MBN) with 1800domain wall (DW) are proposed for stress characterization. The paper also investigates the influence of magnetic domain structure on the statistical properties of MBN for different grain area. It is shown that the root mean square and skewness features of MBN are highly correlated with stress as well as the grain characteristics. Specifically, the interplay between grain boundary (GB), stress and DW dynamics are investigated based on the MBN analysis. Results clearly suggest that the MBN pulses around GB have a significant difference from that in the interiors of grains. GB characteristics, which are various grain shape and orientation, affect the DW dynamics and statistical properties of MBN.

articleTitle: Research on TFM Imaging of Main Pipe Weld of Compound Steel Based on FMC/SMC
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Main pipe weld of compound steel with welding layer of coarse-grained austenitic stainless steel leads to the reduction of image resolution and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) using phased array ultrasonic testing (PAUT). Total focusing method (TFM) can be employed to improve imaging quality, but computational efficiency is influenced significantly by element number. It is very important to balance quality and efficiency of TFM imaging by reasonably choosing array element. Focusing on 75 mm thickness main pipe weld of compound steel having a φ2 mm side-drilled hole in 65 mm, the TFM imaging were compared with data acquisition modes of full matrix capture (FMC) and sparse matrix capture (SMC). The results showed that, with the increasement of element number, the quality of TFM images were both improved. When the element number was 8, compared with FMC-TFM image, the array performance indicator (API) of SMC-TFM image decreased 20% and SNR differed by 0.75dB, while API and SNR were almost the same with 48 elements. The detection result was up to element number and location, so SMC could be utilized to ensure imaging quality and improve computational efficiency in practical inspection.

Author Keywords: Main pipe weld of compound steel

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Affecting Acoustic Emission Detection of Tank Bottom Corrosion
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: With the cost reducing and efficiency increasing background in the oil and gas industry, due to the huge cost advantage, the application of acoustic emission detection technology in storage tank bottom corrosion has gradually expanded. Firstly, the reason of tank bottom corrosion and the influencing factors of bottom plate corrosion detection is introduced in this paper. The different media components are experimentally compared to analyze the acoustic emission characteristics of different media, and the effect of pH on corrosion and the effect of acoustic emission detection are also discussed. Secondly, the impact of distribution distance and height of the acoustic emission sensor are analyzed through the relevant experiments. Finally, other factors that affect the acoustic emission system are briefly introduced. According to the related research, the attention matters in acoustic emission testing is summarized and discussed, which will help the engineer to understand a more particular knowledge of the acoustic emission testing.

articleTitle: Detection and Control Technology of Welding Residual Stress in Railway
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Rail is an important part of the railway track, it directly bears the train loads and interacts with the wheels. Its condition firstly affects the safety and transportation efficiency of train operation. In addition, rail is the most expensive part of the railway track, and the dosage is very large, China's rail production can't meet the need. The annual investment and maintenance costs are also enormous. However, the deformation, rupture and other defects of rails are all related to the stresses in the rail. This article mainly introduces a technology to detect and control the welding residual stress in railway, completes the relevant tensile experiment, testing experiments and controlling experiments, analyses the results and the function of regulation. Eventually, an effective way to detect and reduce the residual stress of rail is found.

articleTitle: Influence of Angled Horizontal Magnetic Field on Guided-Wave Type Transition for EMAT
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Electromagnetic acoustic transducers (EMATs) have been applied to generate guided waves. The type of guided waves in steel plates is transformed as the bias angle of horizontal magnetic field varies. A simple analytical model to predict three transduction mechanisms including Lorentz, magnetization and magnetostriction force has been put forward in this paper. Three coefficients were determined to explain the effect. The experiments on single-coil EMAT presented the echo amplitude distribution of SH guided waves and Lamb waves. It shows that 40° and 70° are the type transition angles. The most efficient generation angle for Lamb waves is 90°, but that for SH guided waves is dependent on the field magnitude.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Induction Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: At the request of the industrial development, induction thermography has emerged as a new nondestructive testing method for surface and subsurface defect detection. However, there exists several problems such as the requirements of excessive excitation power and the limited detection depth. This paper presents a new electrostatic induction thermography NDT method, which can effectively reduce the excitation power and improve the detection depth. Electrostatic induction thermography is based on electrostatic induction effect while using voltage with both positive and negative step to excite and induce current in sample. The sample will be heated up by the induction current and the defect information will be visualized by analysing the thermal pattern. This study investigates excitation source, detection effect and heating depth. In addition, the contrast experiment between pulsed eddy thermography and electrostatic induction thermography has been conducted. It confirms the validity and advantage of the electrostatic induction thermography.

articleTitle: Research on High Speed Phased Array Ultrasonic Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: As the main part of railway, rail's quality has a direct influence on rail transportation safety. At present, conventional ultrasonic technology is commonly used in rail inspection system, however, it exists some shortages such as slow inspection speed, low rail coverage, bad adaption to different rail type and low detection rate. This paper introduces a high-speed rail inspection system, it combines fast ultrasonic phased array technology with high-speed processing algorithm such as expert diagnose algorithm, to improve inspection speed to 100km/h, coverage area of rail and defect detection rate, and can automatically recognize defects, which meet the new requirement of high -speed, high efficiency and high intelligence.

articleTitle: EMAT Phased Array System for Plate Inspection
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: An eight-channel electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT) phased array detection system is designed and a scanning imaging for a defect in an aluminum plate is obtained using this system. Hand-wound racetrack coils with many turns instead of PCB coils with single turn is applied to design the coil structure of the phased array EMATs, and two coil structures are designed. According to simulation results, the sound pressure of the final EMATs is doubled. A transmitting circuit with high power and high delay precision and a receiving circuit with high gain and low noise are designed. Experiments are completed to verify the simulated field directivity of the phased array EMATs and to obtain a sector scanning imaging of a slot defect on the bottom surface of an aluminum plate.

articleTitle: Aging Management System for German Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: This presentation is focused on the aging of mechanical components and the requirements for these components de-scribed in German Nuclear Safety Standards (KTA). Since to the fact that the aging management is closely related to the material degradation and thus on the integrity of the components, advanced nondestructive testing techniques (NDT) must also be available for the inspection of these components. The NDT methods are selected under the consideration of leak before break criteria in pipes and nozzles. With regards to these different needed interdisciplinary faculties, the guarantee for an operational and functional aging management is the task of upper plant management.

articleTitle: Applications of 3D Laser Scanning for Storage Tank: Review, Challenges and Outlook
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: 3D laser scanning technology allows capturing high precision and exceptional density three-dimensional positional information in a limited schedule. Providing an alternative to traditional surveying and measurement methods, this technology has been an active research area in the field of integrity inspection and calibration for storage tank. In this paper, existing literature and case studies on a variety of methods and applications in storage tank were investigated. Meanwhile, limitations and restrictions inherent in traditional instruments that most commonly applied in tank measurement were pointed out. By analyzing current research status and practice progress, some challenging problems for further investigation in practical engineering applications were identified, and an outlook on expected future developments was discussed.

articleTitle: THz Applications for Non-Destructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Up to now THz-TDS-systems aren't considered to be nondestructive testing facilities for large scale industrial applications, despite it was proven that they provide a comprehensive set of quality parameters. A practical approach to bring THz-TDS in addition to already existing testing systems into the industrial mainstream is systematic development of future test procedures and test facilities for dielectrics. For this purpose polyethylene test specimen with introduced artefacts were designed, to evaluate the detection sensitivity of Time of Flight measurements based on dielectrics. SAFT reconstructed tomograms are presented which visualize the sizes and location of artificially introduced flaws.

articleTitle: A Design of Excitation Source for the Optical Lock-In Thermography
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: Optical lock-in thermography is an important non-destructive testing (NDT) method which has been widely used in many industrial applications, such as modern aerospace, renewable energy and nuclear industry. This method has advantages of better signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio and adjustable depth range for defect detection. The excitation source is an important part of the optical lock-in thermography system whose performance has a decisive effect on the defect detection. It is challenging for the design of the excitation source because of wide frequency range requirement (typically 0.01Hz to several hundred kHz) and high power (typ-ically hundreds of W to several kW). This paper presents the design of a novel excitation source with a maximum output power of 2.5kW and a frequency range of 0.01Hz to 100 kHz which is used to drive halogen lamps. The proposed topology, operating principle, the design procedure of the circuit parameters have been described in detail. The essential performance and its effectiveness of the proposed excitation source are demonstrated by an experiment where a lead-steel sample with metal-metal bonded structure has been tested-for validation.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-DOFs Flexible Air-Coupled Ultrasonic Testing System
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of the large-scale complex surface composite testing, a multi-degree-of-freedoms flexible air-coupled ultrasonic testing system is designed by using the mature robot technology and air-coupled technology. Experimental results show that the system can not only meet the requirements of air-coupled detection, but also can use other non-destructive testing techniques such as water-coupled or water-jet-coupling ultrasonic inspection technology to form a variety of reflection and transmission detection systems, which greatly improves the efficiency of inspection and reduces the detection cost.

articleTitle: Ultrasonic Non-Destructive Testing of GRP-Rubber Composites Internal Defects
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: GRP-Rubber composites is widely used in hydroacoustic equipment and ocean exploration. The existence of internal bubbles, degumming and other defects will affect its performance. In this paper, the defect of GRP-Rubber composites is detected by ultrasonic pulse-echo method. 5MHz ultrasonic probe is engaged and multiple imaging methods are adapted to detect. Results shows that all the artificial defects including Φ2mm flat-bottom hole can be detected. Image processing, signal processing and detection gate will also affect the calculation of defect area.

articleTitle: Proceedings of 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (IEEE FENDT 2017)
publicationTitle: 2017 Far East NDT New Technology & Application Forum (FENDT)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: inspection; ultrasonic materials testing; flaw detection; nondestructive testing; eddy current testing; steel; pipes; ultrasonic transducers; finite element analysis; and plates (structures).
